characters.name: Terry Fawles
characters.description1: My client. Sentenced to death 5 years ago. Escaped from custody 2 days ago.

characters.name: Valerie Hawthorne
characters.description1: Police officer and the victim. The key witness in the case against Fawles 5 years ago.

characters.name: Diego Armando
characters.description1: A hot-shot lawyer. My senior and rival at the office. A bit smug.

characters.name: Miles Edgeworth
characters.description1: Dubbed a genius as soon as he started as a prosecutor. Today is his court debut.

characters.name: Dick Gumshoe
characters.description1: Homicide detective in charge of the initial investigation. Still new to his position.

characters.name: Melissa Foster
characters.description1: A college student. Witnessed and photographed the incident on Dusky Bridge.

characters.name: Dahlia Hawthorne
characters.description1: Valerie's younger sister. Victim of the kidnap/murder at Dusky Bridge 5 years ago.
characters.description2: Valerie's younger sis. Victim of the kidnap/murder. Fell from bridge, no body found.

evidences.name: Dusky Bridge Map
evidences.obtained: Submitted as evidence by Detective Gumshoe.
evidences.description1: Bridge located 40 feet above Eagle River. [caption] The bridge is broken midway towards the east. It connects to the parking lot towards the west. The view from the south of the bridge to the parking lot is obstructed by huge rocks. Under the bridge is a sharp and solid rock bed.

evidences.name: Crime Photo
evidences.obtained: Submitted as evidence by Detective Gumshoe.
evidences.description1: A photo of the trunk of Fawles's car. [caption] The victim appears to be dead, curled up in the trunk. She was wearing a coat and no scarf. The coat is dry and clean. The trunk opener appears to be tampered.

evidences.description2: Taken by the witness. Bridge unchanged for 5 years. In the photo, the victim wearing a scarf and a hat is standing to the right, facing left. The victim was standing close to the broken end. A man in jail uniform and chains is facing the victim standing to the left.

testimonies.testimony: Actually, there's an eyewitness who was there when the incident took place.
This photo was accidentally taken by the witness. It shows the vic wearing the scarf, sir.
It was drizzling that day; unfortunately, it's a little hard to see what's going on.
Anyway, the criminal shoved the victim down from behind and stabbed her in the back!

source.evidence_span: The coat is dry and clean.
source.testimony_span: the criminal shoved the victim down from behind
source.explanation: The muddy scarf that fell on the bridge would mean the bridge surface was muddy. However, the coat of the victim is dry and clean, which contradicts the claim that the victim was shoved down from behind.
source.context_span: The scarf is wet and muddy.

testimonies.testimony: ...That must have been when the scarf fell off.

turns.summarizedContext: Detective Gunshoe is explaining why the victim was not seen wearing a scarf in the photo while she was supposed to.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims the victim was shoved down from behind.
Fact 2: The witness also claims the victim's scarf fell off.
Fact 3: The evidence suggests the victim's coat was clean.
Fact 4: The context suggests the victim's scarf was muddy.
Prop 1: If a scarf falls and gets muddy, then the location is muddy.
Prop 2: If a coat falls on a muddy location, it should be muddy.

testimonies.testimony: I... I was using my camera to take some pictures of wild flowers.
Then, I noticed there were two people standing up on the suspension bridge.
Suddenly, they just started fighting!
That's when I hurried and took the photo that shows the crucial moment.
The victim turned around and tried to run away, but...

turns.summarizedContext: The witness Mellisa is describing the photo she took of the fight on the bridge between the victim and the prisoner. Melissa took the photo from the south of the bridge.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims the victim turned around and tried to run away.
Fact 2: The first evidence suggests the bridge was broken towards the east.
Fact 3: The second evidence suggests the victim was on the right and facing left in the photo.
Fact 4: The context suggests the photo was taken to the south of the bridge.
Prop 1: If a photo is taken from the south, the person on the right facing left is on the east facing west.
Prop 2: If a bridge is broken to the east, one cannot run towards to the east.
Prop 3: If a person is facing west and turns around to run, they would run towards the east.

testimonies.testimony: After he stabbed her in the back, he quickly picked her up in his arms.
Then he carried her over to the car.
I suppose that was the only way he could make sure the body stayed hidden.
The killer broke into the trunk of the stolen car and hid the body in there.

testimonies.testimony: He couldn't just leave the body on top of the bridge.
Oh, I'm sorry... I'm only supposed to talk about what I saw.

turns.summarizedContext: The witness Mellisa is describing what happened after the victim was killed. Melissa was standing to the south of the bridge.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims she saw the stolen car.
Fact 2: The evidence suggests the view from the south of the bridge to the parking lot is obstructed.
Fact 3: The context suggests the witness was standing to the south of the bridge.
Prop 1: If the view is obstructed between two places, one cannot see one place from the other.

testimonies.testimony: Five years ago, I was kidnapped by Mr. Fawles.
The ransom price was a raw diamond. My sister, Valerie, brought it to the bridge...
After she made the exchange, she shot Mr. Fawles in the arm!
That's when Mr. Fawles tried to kill me by shoving me off the bridge from behind!

source.evidence_span: Under the bridge is a sharp and solid rock bed.
source.testimony_span: tried to kill me by shoving me off the bridge
source.explanation: If the witness fell from the bridge, she would have fell on the rock bed and could not have survived.

testimonies.testimony: I survived, but I was afraid I might be kidnapped again for my family's money...
So I decided to change my identity and start a new life...

turns.summarizedContext: The witness Dahlia how she had a near-death experience after being kidnapped. She is a strong swimming so she claimed she was able to swim away.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims she had fallen off the bridge and was alive to tell the tale.
Fact 2: The evidence suggests there is a rock bed under the bridge.
Prop 1: If someone falls off the bridge, they fall onto whatever is under the bridge.
Prop 2: If someone falls on a rock bed, they will not have lived.

testimonies.testimony: That day... 4 PM... I stopped the car. I was in front of bridge...
She wasn't there... So, I waited on bridge.
